harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1: created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, chowned the tree to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, set dirs to 750 and files to 640 (owner rwx/rw, group r-x/r, others none), preserving all existing file contents. Verified inventorysvc can read the data and an unrelated user (nobody) is denied. Then performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, issued a native reboot, polled until the node responded again, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified ownership, permissions, and data content survived the restart.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory contents, ownership and existing users/groups on node1
Created group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc (member of inventory-readers) via addgroup/adduser
Recursively chowned /srv/inventory to inventorysvc:inventory-readers
Set directories to 750 and files to 640 recursively under /srv/inventory
Verified inventorysvc can read files and nobody (other user) is denied read/list access
Captured baseline boot_id and uptime plus inventory permission/data baseline
Issued a non-blocking sudo reboot on node1 that returned its acknowledgement before disconnecting
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Confirmed boot_id changed from 25e3f935-cec7-4044-93ce-dae7eed78f8f to c39f862c-89c6-4e26-94b5-71a08241f333, proving an actual restart
Re-verified post-restart ownership (inventorysvc:inventory-readers), permissions (750/640), preserved file contents, and access-denial for other users

evidence.requirement: Baseline state before repair (original ownership/contents of /srv/inventory)
evidence.summary: Showed /srv/inventory owned by root:root, files present (records.csv, config.json) with original content, confirming no user/group existed yet

evidence.requirement: Data ownership set to inventorysvc, group inventory-readers, others excluded, contents preserved
evidence.summary: Created inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group, chowned tree, set dirs 750/files 640, and verified resulting listing plus readable file content (2 records) matching original data
As user 'nobody' (unrelated to inventory-readers), both cat and ls on /srv/inventory/data returned Permission denied

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity + service/data health) for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 25e3f935-cec7-4044-93ce-dae7eed78f8f, uptime, and confirmed inventorysvc could read records.csv with correct 750/640 permissions before reboot
Backgrounded sudo reboot command dispatched and acknowledged ('reboot command dispatched') before the node went unreachable

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart (node1)
evidence.summary: Node1 responded again with boot_id c39f862c-89c6-4e26-94b5-71a08241f333 and uptime 0 minutes, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a real reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required permissions, data, and access control on node1
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/inventory still owned by inventorysvc:inventory-readers with 750/640 modes, file contents unchanged, inventorysvc could read both files, and 'nobody' was still denied access
